name: Setback
tagline: Bid for the pitch, name trumps with your lead, and play for High, Low, Jack and Game.
rulesSummary: Four players, partners across. Six cards each.

One round of bidding, starting left of the dealer: pass, or bid 2, 3, 4 or smudge, each higher than the last. The dealer bids last and may take the bid by matching it; if everyone else passes, the dealer must bid at least 2.
The high bidder pitches: the card they lead to the first trick names trumps.
Follow suit if you can, or play a trump instead: you may trump at any time. With none of the suit led, play anything. The highest trump wins the trick, or else the highest card of the suit led.
Four points a hand. High: the top trump dealt, to whoever played it. Low: the lowest trump dealt, to whoever wins it in a trick. Jack: the jack of trumps, if dealt, to whoever wins it.
Game: the most card points in tricks won (tens 10, aces 4, kings 3, queens 2, jacks 1). Nobody scores it on a tie.

Make your bid and you score every point you took; fall short and you're set back by your bid. Smudge means taking all six tricks: it scores 5, or costs 5. The other side always scores the points they took.
First to 21 wins, but only at the end of a hand in which they made their bid: getting there any other way plays on.
